Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py
  tests/test_stall_failclosed.py
  tests/test_pipeline_queue.py

THE DEFECT, measured on the live module today. is_stalled reads the last guest
response from a fixed key list ("last_response_at", "last_response",
"last_response_date"). Three probes, same episode shape, now = 2026-08-03:

  last_response_at = 30 days ago, follow_up_date set  -> (True, 'no response for 14 days')   CORRECT
  last_guest_response_at = 30 days ago, same          -> (False, '')                         WRONG
  no response field at all, follow_up_date set        -> (False, '')                         DANGEROUS

The OR logic is right. The problem is what happens when the silence signal is
ABSENT or lives under an unrecognised key: the check is silently skipped and the
episode is reported HEALTHY. That reads absence of evidence as evidence that the
guest replied.

WHY IT MATTERS. The in-flight count drives the owner's only alert. His named
subtle failure is "queue count looks healthy but is fake: six episodes in flight
where three are stalled guests who ghosted; the number reassures while the
pipeline is dry". An episode whose response tracking is missing or differently
named counts as healthy forever and no alert ever fires. This is the exact
failure the module exists to prevent, reachable through a typo in a field name.

THE FIX — fail closed on unknown silence:
1. When NO last-response value can be found under any recognised key, the
   silence signal is UNKNOWN. Unknown must NOT be treated as "responded
   recently". Return stalled True with a reason naming it explicitly, for
   example "no response data recorded; treating as stalled (fail-closed)". Add
   a comment recording the measured incident and the rationale: an episode we
   cannot prove is alive must not inflate the count that triggers the owner's
   only alert.
2. Widen the recognised key list to include the variants actually used by
   callers in this repo. Search the repo for the keys that carry a guest's last
   reply before choosing the list, and note in a comment which callers you
   found. Include "last_guest_response_at".
3. Provide an explicit escape hatch so a genuinely-new episode is not
   mis-flagged: when the episode carries a truthy field indicating no reply is
   expected yet (choose a clear name such as "awaiting_first_contact" and
   document it), unknown silence does NOT stall. This must be an explicit
   opt-out on the episode, never an inferred default.
4. Do not change the existing OR rule, the recorded-stage exemption, or any
   threshold. This change is only about the unknown case and key coverage.

TESTS (tests/test_stall_failclosed.py; at least 5):
 (1) THE DANGEROUS CASE: an episode with a follow-up date and NO response field
     at all is stalled, and the reason names fail-closed;
 (2) an episode using the key "last_guest_response_at" 30 days ago IS stalled,
     proving key coverage;
 (3) NEGATIVE: an episode explicitly marked awaiting_first_contact with no
     response data is NOT stalled, so a brand-new booking is not mis-flagged;
 (4) NEGATIVE: the healthy case still passes: a recent response under any
     recognised key plus a firm follow-up date is not stalled;
 (5) the existing OR rule is intact: no firm date alone still stalls, and
     14 days of silence alone still stalls;
 (6) an already-recorded episode is still exempt from guest-silence stalling;
 (7) queue counting reflects the change: a world of three episodes where one has
     no response data reports count 2, not 3.
Keep tests/test_pipeline_queue.py green; if a fixture relied on the old
silently-healthy behaviour, UPDATE it with a one-line comment citing this
incident.
